nota: Promedios de grupo PUBLICADOS de astronautas; no son una predicción para ninguna persona. Cada cifra se copió de la fuente el 2026-11-15 (PubMed/NASA); ver docs/politica-de-datos.md.

items.n: 21 astronauts, 13 ISS missions, 3,248 in-flight days (wrist actigraphy)
items.en_vuelo: 6.09 h per night (SD 0.67) obtained on the ISS
items.referencia: 6.41 h (SD 0.65) about 3 months before launch · 6.95 h (SD 1.04) in the first week after return
items.lectura: The same astronauts obtained 6.41 h about three months before launch: part of the shortfall predates flight.

items.n: 6 male astronauts, 2–6 months on the ISS (finger arterial pressure)
items.en_vuelo: no change in heart rate or blood pressure compared with pre-flight; high-frequency power of the beat-to-beat interval and stroke volume were reduced in flight
items.referencia: after return, seated: 60.0 ± 9.4 vs 54.9 ± 9.6 beats/min before flight
items.lectura: Small sample (6 men) and a single study: a published expectation, not a rule.
items.fuente: Hughson et al. 2012, J Appl Physiol 112(5):719–727

items.n: NASA Human Research Program, risk page
items.en_vuelo: on average, bones lose between 1% and 1.5% of their density each month during four-to-six-month missions
items.referencia: not one of the six official indicators; shown because it is the best-documented body change of flight
items.fuente: NASA HRP — Risk of Spaceflight-Induced Bone Changes
